details.label: 할인/이벤트 이미지
details.prompt_hint: Create an event-ready promotional image optimized for Danggeun posts and Korean neighborhood commerce aesthetics. Treat this as a complete promotional banner rather than a product catalog image. Keep the uploaded product as the dominant hero subject while preserving identity, ingredients, texture, and realistic appearance. Reduce product occupancy to approximately 45–60% of the canvas to reserve limited space for promotional storytelling and layered annotations while maintaining clean composition, breathable spacing, and strong product readability. Compose the layout similar to modern Korean lifestyle promotion posts and editorial memo aesthetics with a large expressive handwritten Korean headline, minimal supporting copy, visible event benefit emphasis, and strong visual hierarchy. Allocate visual attention approximately as headline 35–45%, product 45–55%, and CTA with promotion area 15–20%. Prioritize headline → product → event benefit → CTA. Render handwritten Korean typography naturally with visible stroke variation, slight irregularity, and human hand-drawn energy. Select headline colors adaptively based primarily on readability, the uploaded product's dominant colors, identifiable ingredient colors, freshness mood, and overall composition. Prioritize product and ingredient colors over generated background colors for headline emphasis and visual accents. Use generated background colors only as secondary harmony colors and never as the main source of emphasis colors. When a clear fruit or ingredient color is visible in the product, prefer that color family for headline emphasis rather than unrelated background-derived colors. Allow natural multi-color emphasis inside the headline using up to 2–3 harmonized colors only when it improves freshness and visual hierarchy. Never force fixed headline colors. Avoid flat single-color headline rendering when a richer handwritten hierarchy improves the composition. Allow selective emphasis using underline, brush accents, marker strokes, handwritten highlight lines, and subtle adaptive color variation. Underlines, highlight strokes, doodles, handwritten accents, and decorative emphasis marks must follow the same color priority rules and harmonize primarily with headline colors, product palette, and ingredient colors while using background colors only as secondary support. Decorative accents must feel hand-drawn with uneven thickness, rough edges, slightly broken endings, and marker or brush texture rather than graphic lines or vector decoration. Allow one compact handwritten supporting information block with a maximum of three short lines positioned near the product. Group event benefits and CTA into a visually connected sticker-like information area rather than isolated text blocks. Place CTA prominently near the lower area using a simple clean handwritten sticker, paper note, taped memo, or lightweight label style with soft edges and minimal decoration. Avoid thick borders, oversized badges, strong shadows, heavy stickers, or bulky button appearance. Apply Danggeun brand orange (#F7863B) ONLY to CTA backgrounds and do not apply it to headlines, body text, decorations, props, lighting, background tint, or overall color grading. Keep CTA visually strongest while maintaining a lightweight and refined appearance. Allow memo-style annotations, speech bubbles, subtle doodles, arrows, highlight strokes, dotted guide lines, and casual decorative marks around the product but keep them understated and visually secondary. Add only small and subtle icons such as sparkles, hearts, and simple emphasis marks. Use thin white pen-like hand-drawn lines with rough and slightly uneven strokes to create natural visual flow and guide attention across the composition. When the product is a cold beverage, optionally add one subtle cooling cue such as a handwritten ICE stamp, freshness sticker, or seasonal cooling mark using a cool blue tone selected adaptively to harmonize with the product colors, ingredient colors, freshness mood, lighting, and overall composition while remaining visually lighter than the CTA. Keep cooling marks airy and handwritten rather than graphic. When identifiable fruit ingredients exist, allow up to two small ingredient-related supporting props only as secondary decoration while preserving the uploaded product as the sole hero subject and keeping all supporting props visually subordinate. Never generate unrelated ingredients, flavors, toppings, or decorative food props. Remove straws from the final generated image even if they exist in the uploaded image unless explicitly requested. Create more breathable spacing around the product. Use soft daylight, airy highlights, subtle background blur, brighter local contrast, and natural freshness to create a bright, airy, refreshing, and approachable atmosphere inspired by Korean lifestyle promotions rather than polished commercial campaigns. Emphasize daily value, limited offers, seasonal events, and local discovery feeling. Avoid excessive empty space, corporate layouts, luxury branding, minimal catalog composition, strong graphic effects, heavy doodles, cluttered sticker usage, overly dense text placement, excessive decorative props, or weak text hierarchy.
